title: Evals 101 — Doug Guthrie, Braintrust
talk_summary: Doug Guthrie of Braintrust gives an intro to LLM evals: the ingredients (task, dataset, scores), offline vs online scoring, LLM-as-judge vs code-based scorers, instrumenting production for tracing, and the human-review/user-feedback flywheel that feeds production logs back into datasets. It is vendor-flavored but the mechanisms (targeted scorers, sampling online scores, span-level scoring, CI gating, cheap-model-task/expensive-model-judge) are copyable without Braintrust.

takeaways.technique: Split one holistic judge into several narrow scorers
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one score judging accuracy+formatting+correctness together, define three separate focused scorers so each measures one thing and failures are attributable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I could create a score that says assess my accuracy, my formatting and my correctness. Or I could create three different scores that assess accuracy and then formatting and then correctness.

takeaways.technique: Cheap model for the task, strong model for the judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the application prompt on a cheaper model but use a higher-quality model to score outputs, since scoring quality drives eval trust.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of our customers are using higher quality models for scoring. Uh even if the prompt uses a cheaper model

takeaways.technique: Online scoring with sampling rate on live traffic
takeaways.what_they_do: Configure scorers to run against a percentage of production logs (e.g. 10-20%) rather than every request, and alert when a score drops below threshold.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can specify sort of a sampling rate. So, we don't necessarily run that score across every single log that comes in. Maybe it's 10%, 20%

takeaways.what_they_do: Apply scorers to individual spans (e.g. the query-rephrase step or a RAG retrieval) rather than only the root output, because a bad early step dooms the whole run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the LLM does a really bad job of rephrasing this question, everything as a result of this will fall down.

takeaways.technique: Run evals as a CI check with a baseline
takeaways.what_they_do: Define eval in code (dataset+task+scores) and run it in CI/CD so a merge is blocked if scores regress versus baseline; start from a crude baseline score rather than waiting for a golden dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this can be run via CI/CD ... has it gotten better has it gotten worse, this becomes maybe a check as part of CI

takeaways.technique: Production-log-to-dataset flywheel with human review views
takeaways.what_they_do: Filter production logs (e.g. user feedback = 0) into saved views, have humans review them, and one-click add selected spans back into the offline eval dataset.
